title: Introduce reusable CI smoke harness + lightweight workflows for RAG quickstarts
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Adds a small, low-cost CI smoke suite for RAG quickstarts: reusable GH Actions templates and a zero-dependency smoke runner that validates basic indexing, retrieval, and a single tool-call assertion. Maintainers can opt-in per quickstart.
description:
Motivation: many quickstarts lacked a deterministic CI guard which allowed trivial regressions (index format drift, env var mismatches, startup races) to reach main. This PR introduces a deliberately small smoke harness and reusable GitHub Actions templates so maintainers can opt their quickstarts into a quick end-to-end verification on PRs. The harness intentionally verifies surface-level contracts (indexing completes, a canonical query returns an expected snippet, tool-call stubs are invoked) rather than correctness of all features.

What this PR contains: - .github/workflows/ci-templates/rag-smoke.yml: a templated workflow that can be included by each quickstart to run smoke checks. Supports a small matrix (node14/python3.10) and a label-based opt-out (ci/skip-smoke). - quickstarts/ci-playbooks/smoke-runner.sh: POSIX shell script with no runtime deps beyond curl and jq (jq usage guarded; falls back to basic string checks). Bootstraps a tiny ephemeral index, invokes the example quickstart CLI/server, and asserts expected outputs with conservative timeouts. - quickstarts/ci-playbooks/sample-index.json: deterministic 3-doc corpus used for smoke runs. - quickstarts/ci-playbooks/README.md: maintainer guide showing how to include the template, required env vars, and OWNERS opt-in process. - quickstarts/examples/minirag/ci-assertions.txt: minimal assertion set for the Node quickstart example. - docs/quickstarts/ci-guide.md: cross-referenced guide for troubleshooting failed smoke runs. - Makefile: added ci-smoke target to run the harness locally.

Engineering notes: initial CI run surfaced a startup race in the Python quickstart container; I added a 45s healthcheck loop and a small reduction of container setup commands to keep Action runtime under quota. I also added --max-time curl flags and an environment variable to tune timeouts for slow runners. The harness is intentionally shallow and short-lived to reduce compute cost and flakiness.

Security/cost considerations: smoke index is tiny and synthetic; workflows do not persist secrets. For private quickstarts that require external credentials the README documents a manual opt-in path and how to configure ephemeral secrets in GH Actions.

How to review: focus on the README for clarity, the workflow template for matrix/opt-out correctness, and the smoke-runner.sh for robust retry/backoff behavior. Suggested follow-ups: containerized runner images for heavier quickstarts and a publisher/consumer contract file for assertion standardization.
